summary: MOOD V2 Phase 1 frontend-only regression for ForceUpdateGate + AuthContext entitlement wiring. App launches with NO crash/white screen, ForceUpdateGate correctly FAILS OPEN (GET /api/config returns update_check_enabled=false, no 'Update Required' shown), landing page renders normally, Terms & Privacy modal works, login with moodtester/MoodTest1234567 succeeds (POST /api/auth/login → 200), home tabs render after login, GET /api/me/entitlement IS called on token change. HOWEVER two issues were uncovered: (1) BLOCKER for normal preview access — frontend EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://wearable-stats-hub.preview.emergentagent.com but that host returns 404 for ALL /api/* paths in this forked env; the live backend is on https://app-refine-1.preview.emergentagent.com. Test was completed by route-rewriting wearable-stats-hub→app-refine-1 in playwright. (2) NEW BUG in V2 Phase 1 wiring — AuthContext.refreshEntitlement() calls apiFetch('/api/me/entitlement') but utils/api.ts apiFetch does NOT attach the Authorization Bearer header, so the call returns 403 'Not authenticated' on every login. /api/users/me works because it uses raw fetch with explicit Authorization header. Verified via curl with the same fresh token that /api/me/entitlement returns 200 with full payload. Net effect: server entitlement is never loaded; SubscriptionContext silently falls back to local cache. App still renders (fails soft as designed) but server-authoritative entitlement is effectively dead. Deprecated packages detected: expo-av (Video + Audio) still imported in index.tsx, create-post.tsx, ExerciseLookupSheet.tsx, SmartVideoPlayer.tsx — migration to expo-video is partial.

integration_issues.flow: AuthContext entitlement fetch after login (V2 Phase 1)
integration_issues.issue: GET /api/me/entitlement returns 403 'Not authenticated' because contexts/AuthContext.tsx:498 uses apiFetch() which (utils/api.ts:31) does NOT attach the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Direct curl with the same token returns 200 with the full entitlement payload, proving the endpoint and token are valid. Fix: pass headers explicitly, e.g. apiFetch<Entitlement>('/api/me/entitlement', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${storedToken}` } }), OR upgrade utils/api.ts to auto-attach the stored auth token. Impact: server entitlement is never set; SubscriptionContext silently falls back to local cache for hasActiveAccess.

integration_issues.issue: frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://wearable-stats-hub.preview.emergentagent.com but that hostname returns 404 for every /api/* path in this forked preview env (verified 5x). critical_code_review_comments: utils/api.ts apiFetch is the documented helper but silently omits auth — any caller that doesn't manually pass headers gets unauthenticated requests. This is a footgun; the new V2 Phase 1 entitlement code is the first victim. Recommend centralizing auth-header injection in apiFetch.
contexts/AuthContext.tsx:491-505 refreshEntitlement reads storedToken purely to early-return; it never sends the token with the request. The intent of the code clearly assumes apiFetch attaches it.
ForceUpdateGate correctly fails open on /api/config error — verified behavior matches spec.

rca_of_issue: Entitlement 403 RCA: contexts/AuthContext.tsx line 498 calls `apiFetch<Entitlement>('/api/me/entitlement')`. The utils/api.ts implementation (lines 31-46) builds fetch headers as `{ 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...options.headers }` — no Authorization is added and the caller passes no headers. Backend dependency requires Bearer token → returns 403 Not authenticated. Reproduction: log in via UI → observe network panel showing GET /api/me/entitlement 403 while GET /api/users/me (separate raw fetch on line 265 that explicitly sets Authorization) returns 200 with the same just-issued token. Curl with the issued token returns 200 from /api/me/entitlement. Mitigation options: (a) pass headers in the call site: apiFetch('/api/me/entitlement', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${storedToken}` } }); (b) preferable long-term — make utils/api.ts apiFetch auto-attach the auth token from secureStorage so all current and future callers are safe by default.
